This is a province-wide utility page, not an area page and not a listing feed: headed "BC Tenancy & Landlord Forms: RTB Guide | Jared Gibbons" (body title "BC Landlord & Tenant Resources: RTB Forms Explained"; "Last reviewed: October 2, 2026"), it explains Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB) forms and rules form by form for landlords, tenants, and people buying or selling a rental property in BC, with a "general information, not legal advice" disclaimer and an eight-question closing FAQ.
Streets, schools and getting around BC Landlord Tenant Resources

items.t: Scope: all of British Columbia under the Residential Tenancy Act — there are no streets, edges or sub-area boundaries for this page, and no condo stock "concentrates" anywhere for it; its geography is the province. Manufactured home park tenancies sit under the separate Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and are not this page's subject.

Structure as read: an "At a glance" strip (2026 rent increase limit 2.3%, 2.2% in 2027; at least 3 full months' written notice for a rent increase on form RTB-7; security and pet damage deposits each capped at half the first month's rent; 15 days to return deposits after the forwarding address is received in writing); a quick-reference index of the RTB-1, RTB-27, RTB-22, RTB-7, RTB-52, RTB-30, RTB-33, RTB-32L/32P, RTB-29, RTB-8, RTB-47 and RTB-12 series forms; then sections on starting a tenancy, deposits, rent increases, repairs and maintenance, ending a tenancy, dispute resolution, and buying or selling a tenanted property; and a Sources list of fifteen RTB/gov.bc.ca pages plus the Residential Tenancy Act on BC Laws.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in BC Landlord Tenant Resources

items.t: : a security deposit can be no more than half of the first month's rent, and a pet damage deposit the same cap, no matter how many pets, with no pet damage deposit for certified guide or service dogs and no other pet fees; a landlord cannot keep a deposit without the tenant's written permission or an RTB order; once the landlord has the tenant's forwarding address in writing (form RTB-47), the deposits must be returned with any interest within 15 days if there are no issues, failing which the tenant can apply through the direct request process and the landlord may be ordered to pay double; deposit interest for 2026 is 0% per the page. Deposit interest owed for years before 2026 at a year-by-year level: Not confirmed — the page states the 2026 rate and points to the RTB calculator, and no year-by-year table was opened.

: a landlord can end a tenancy only for reasons allowed under the Residential Tenancy Act, on the correct form, in writing, signed and dated, with the unit address, effective date and reason; eviction notices cannot be served by text message. RTB-30 (10 Day Notice for Unpaid Rent or Utilities — tenant has 5 days to pay or dispute); RTB-33 (One Month Notice for Cause — tenant has 10 days to dispute); RTB-32L / RTB-32P (Three Month Notice for landlord's use / purchaser's use — these must be generated through the RTB web portal and a non-generated notice is legally unenforceable; 3 months' notice, 21 days to dispute, one month's rent compensation, the person moving in must live in the unit at least 12 months, and personal-occupancy notices are not allowed in some buildings with 5 or more rental units); RTB-29 (Four Month Notice for Demolition or Conversion — permits/approvals required, 30 days to dispute, one month's rent compensation; major renovations or repairs are a separate process requiring an RTB order of possession).

: no RTB form is required for a tenant's own notice, which must be in writing with name, date, unit address, move-out date and signature, and for a month-to-month tenancy must be received at least one full rental month before the effective date and before the day rent is due; a fixed-term tenancy cannot be ended early by tenant's notice alone except in specific situations. On form RTB-8 (Mutual Agreement to End a Tenancy) neither side can be required to sign, mutual agreement carries neither side's notice compensation, and a text message is not a legal way to end a tenancy by mutual agreement.

Strata rental position — the condo-specific overlay: a rented strata condo carries two rule sets at once. The tenancy itself runs under the Residential Tenancy Act frame above; the strata layer cannot add a long-term rental ban, because rental-restriction bylaws have been VOID since November 24, 2022 for strata property anywhere in BC — any directory or older bylaw line saying "rentals not allowed" is void for long-term rentals and must not be read as current law; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.

Pad rent (parks, regime boundary only): pad rent for a manufactured home site tenancy is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the rates above: the rent increase limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, with 3 full months' notice and one increase per 12 months.

Currency of the forms: the RTB updates its forms, and the page directs readers to download the current version from the official RTB Tenancy forms page; whether each form number and version described on the page is still the current published version at rebuild time is not confirmed — it is a per-form check against the RTB forms page.

blocks.text: Good to know about BC Landlord Tenant Resources

items.t: A downloaded RTB-32P is worthless paper. RTB-32L and RTB-32P personal-use notices must be generated through the RTB web portal, and the RTB position as cited on the page is that a notice other than a generated one is legally unenforceable — generate it in the portal, give the full 3 months, and budget the one month's rent compensation.

Personal-use notices are barred in some larger rental buildings. As the page states it, personal-occupancy notices are not allowed in some buildings with 5 or more rental units — a condo buyer counting on an RTB-32P in such a building needs that check before writing, not after.
Deposit interest for 2026 is 0% — earlier years are a calculator question.
The page is dated, and the forms move.
Two rental regimes share one percentage by coincidence.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in BC Landlord Tenant Resources

items.t: : RTB-30 (10 Day Notice for Unpaid Rent or Utilities — tenant has 5 days to pay or dispute); RTB-33 (One Month Notice for Cause — 10 days to dispute); RTB-32L / RTB-32P (Three Month Notice for landlord's use / purchaser's use — these must be generated through the RTB web portal and a non-generated notice is legally unenforceable; 3 months' notice, 21 days to dispute, one month's rent compensation, the person moving in must live in the unit at least 12 months, and personal-occupancy notices are not allowed in some buildings with 5 or more rental units); RTB-29 (Four Month Notice for Demolition or Conversion — permits/approvals required, 30 days to dispute, one month's rent compensation). Eviction notices cannot be served by text message.

MHPTA pad-rent block — regime boundary only: pad rent for a manufactured home site tenancy is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the rates above; the limits are Act percentages ONLY — 2026 = 2.3% plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees; 2027 = 2.2% plus the proportional amount — on 3 full months' notice, once every 12 months.

Strata block (where a tenanted unit is a strata lot, incl. a bare-land strata lot): rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023.
PTT — worked example (inputs + tier math, general tiers only): Tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000.

GST on vacant land — CRA GI-003 level only (kept distinct from tenanted-property sales): developer/business sales and newly subdivided lots generally TAXABLE; an individual's sale of personal-use land generally exempt. Finer points not confirmed. The FTHB GST rebate is new HOUSING, not bare land (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, CRA governs; 100% to $1M phasing to $1.5M, max $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year.

faq.q: How much can a landlord charge for deposits?
faq.a: A security deposit of no more than half the first month's rent, and — if pets are allowed — a pet damage deposit of no more than half the first month's rent regardless of the number of pets; once the landlord has the tenant's forwarding address in writing (form RTB-47), the deposits, with any interest, must be returned within 15 days if there are no issues, and a landlord cannot keep any of a deposit without the tenant's written permission or an RTB order.

faq.q: I am buying a tenanted condo — does the tenancy end on completion?
faq.a: No: a landlord cannot end a tenancy just because they want to sell; on a sale the buyer becomes the new landlord and the tenancy continues on the same terms. Only once all conditions of sale are met can a purchaser who intends to live in the unit (or have a close family member live there) ask the seller in writing to give a Three Month Notice (RTB-32P), which must be generated through the RTB web portal — a non-generated notice is legally unenforceable.

faq.q: Can the strata stop me renting out a condo I buy?
faq.a: Not by a long-term rental-restriction bylaw — those bylaws have been void province-wide since November 24, 2022, whatever an older bylaw text or a building directory says. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and the tenancy itself must still follow the Residential Tenancy Act frame in.

faq.q: I am buying a tenanted townhome — does the tenancy end on completion?
faq.a: No: a landlord cannot end a tenancy just because they want to sell; on a sale the buyer becomes the new landlord and the tenancy continues on the same terms.

faq.q: Can the strata stop me renting out a townhome I buy?
faq.a: Not by a long-term rental-restriction bylaw — those bylaws have been void province-wide since November 24, 2022, whatever an older bylaw text or a building directory says.

faq.q: Does the 2.3% limit also cap manufactured home pad rent?
faq.a: Not on its own: a manufactured home site tenancy sits under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, whose limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus the proportional amount for 2027, on 3 full months' notice once every 12 months.

faq.q: How much can a landlord charge for deposits?
faq.a: A security deposit of no more than half the first month's rent, and a pet damage deposit of no more than half the first month's rent regardless of the number of pets; once the landlord has the tenant's forwarding address in writing, the deposits (with any interest) must be returned within 15 days if there are no issues.

faq.q: Can I download an RTB-32P and serve it?
faq.a: No — RTB-32L and RTB-32P must be generated through the RTB web portal, and a non-generated notice is legally unenforceable; budget the full 3 months and the one month's rent compensation.

faq.q: How much can rent be increased in BC in 2026?
faq.a: Up to 2.3% for a residential tenancy (the published 2027 limit is 2.2%), only once every 12 months, on at least 3 full months' written notice on form RTB-7; anything above the limit needs an RTB-52 arbitrator application or the tenant's voluntary written agreement (RTB Rent increases page, as cited on the live page).

faq.q: Can a landlord end a tenancy because the property is being sold?
faq.a: No: the tenancy continues and the buyer becomes the new landlord. Only once all conditions of sale are met can a purchaser who intends to live in the unit (or have a close family member live there) ask the seller in writing to give a Three Month Notice (RTB-32P), which must be generated through the RTB web portal (RTB Sell a rental property page, as cited on the live page).

faq.q: What form starts a tenancy, and when must the tenant get a copy?
faq.a: Form RTB-1, the Residential Tenancy Agreement — or an equivalent agreement containing all the standard terms the Residential Tenancy Act requires. The landlord must give the tenant a copy within 21 days of signing (RTB Tenancy agreements page, as cited on the live page).
